title: When THE CHRONICLER meets THE RAGPICKER:
subtitle: The Storm from Paradise

script.text: In a ruined chamber where the wind howls through shattered windows, two figures sit before a chessboard. The table appears transparent, a marvel of mechanical engineering.

One player is THE CHRONICLER (representing Historicism/Social Democracy). He wears the robes of a scribe and holds a rosary of beads. He believes history is a sequence of events, moving inevitably toward a better future.

script.speaker: THE Chronicler
script.text: It is your move

script.speaker: THE Chronicler
script.text: Though the outcome is certain. The tide of Progress is with me. I simply recount what happened, adding day to day, bead to bead. I empathize with the victors, for they carry the cultural heritage. Time is a river, and we are swimming with the current

The other player is THE RAGPICKER (representing Historical Materialism/Benjamin). He is disheveled, his eyes wide with horror, his pockets full of debris. He does not see a river; he sees a pile of wreckage.

script.speaker: THE Ragpicker
script.text: You are a fool

script.speaker: THE Ragpicker
script.text: You think you are playing a machine called History. But look inside my table
The Ragpicker reveals the secret: a hunchbacked dwarf named Theology sits hidden inside the apparatus, pulling the strings of the puppet called Materialism.

script.speaker: THE RAGPICKER
script.text: I cannot win without him

script.speaker: THE Ragpicker
script.text: He is small and ugly and must be kept out of sight, but he is the grandmaster. You play for the future. I play for the past
The Chronicler points to a painting on the wall: Paul Klee's Angelus Novus.

script.speaker: THE Chronicler
script.text: A lovely image

script.speaker: THE Chronicler
script.text: An angel flying toward the future
cries The Ragpicker.

script.speaker: THE RAGPICKER
script.text: Look at his eyes. He is staring backward. Where you see a chain of events, he sees one single catastrophe which keeps piling wreckage upon wreckage and hurls it in front of his feet. He wants to stay, awaken the dead, and make whole what has been smashed. But a storm is blowing from Paradise. It has caught his wings with such violence he cannot close them. The storm propels him into the future to which his back is turned, while the pile of debris before him grows sky-high. This storm is what we call progress
The wind shakes the room. The Chronicler clutches his beads.

script.speaker: THE WIND
script.text: But we must trust in the unfolding of time. The arc of history bends toward justice

script.speaker: THE CHRONICLER
script.text: Time is not empty

script.speaker: THE Ragpicker
script.text: Time is filled by the Jetztzeit—the Here-and-Now. Every second is the narrow gate through which the Messiah might enter
The Ragpicker stands up. He grabs a pistol and points it not at The Chronicler, but at the clock tower visible through the window.

script.speaker: THE RAGPICKER
script.text: The enemy has not ceased to be victorious
, The Ragpicker warns.

script.speaker: THE RAGPICKER
script.text: And not even the dead will be safe if he wins. We do not need to recount the past "as it really was." We need to seize a memory as it flashes up at a moment of danger. We need to blast the epoch out of the reified continuity of history
He fires at the clock. The hands stop. The ticking ceases.

script.speaker: THE CLOCK
script.text: I am not here to add to your rosary

script.speaker: THE Ragpicker
script.text: I am here to pull the emergency brake
script.action: declares, brushing the chessboard against the grain, scattering the pieces
